consumer_examinations.affected_use:
**(c) Phase system.** The **phase system** of the model is the first-order
system on the open set $I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$
with right-hand side
$$G_{F}(t,x,v):=\Bigl(v,\ \frac{F(t,x,v)}{m}\Bigr),$$
read as a system of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]];
its state variable is $z=(x,v)$. For an interval $J\subseteq I_0$ with
nonempty interior, a **phase solution** on $J$ means a differentiable curve
$z:J\to Q\times\mathbb R$ satisfying $z'(t)=G_F(t,z(t))$ for every $t\in J$,
with domain-relative derivatives at included endpoints. Equivalently, for
any $t_0\in J$ it is a solution in the cited IVP sense with datum
$(t_0,z(t_0))$. For a $C^2$ curve $x:J\to Q$, being a motion is equivalent
to $t\mapsto(x(t),x'(t))$ being a phase solution: the first component is
$x'=v$ and the second is $x''=F(t,x,x')/m$. Conversely a phase solution
$(x,v)$ has $x'=v$ and $v'=F(t,x,v)/m$; continuity of $F$ makes $v'$ continuous,
so $x$ is $C^2$ and is a motion. This is the argument of clause (c) of
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] read in one
coordinate. Here $x$ is the **position** or **displacement** coordinate and
$v$ the **velocity** coordinate; both are read in the fixed inertial frame in
which the model is declared. The phase system inherits the standing
regularity: $G_{F}$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable
locally uniformly in time, so the Picard–Lindelöf hypotheses of
[[thm-picard-lindelof-local-existence-and-uniqueness]] hold at every point of
its domain.

**(i) The model class.** A **stability model** is a force model of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N\ge1$ labels, fixed masses
$m_1,\dots,m_N>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), a time window
$I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ that is a nondegenerate open interval and an open
configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]). Its full force
map $F_0$ has domain
$D_0:=I_0\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, exactly as in clause (iii) of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]. Put
$\mathsf M:=\operatorname{diag}(m_1I_3,\dots,m_NI_3)$ and define the full
first-order field
$$Z_0:D_0\to\mathbb R^{6N},\qquad Z_0(t,x,v):=\bigl(v,\mathsf M^{-1}F_0(t,x,v)\bigr).$$
The page may specify an open restriction
domain $D\subseteq D_0$ and then uses $F:=F_0|_D$; every force evaluation in
the statements below is on this restriction. This is still a restriction of
the supplier's full force map, not a force map with a different domain. The
associated field on this restriction is $Z:=Z_0|_D$. The
**motions** are the $C^2$ curves $x:J\to Q$, where $J\subseteq I_0$ is a time
interval, of [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] for which $(t,x(t),x'(t))\in D$ and
$m_ix_i''(t)=F_i(t,x(t),x'(t))$. For any declared open domain
$D\subseteq D_0$, including $D=D_0$, call such a
motion **$D$-maximal** when it has no extension to a strictly larger interval
whose state curve remains in $D$; this is the maximal-solution notion for the
first-order ODE $z'=Z(t,z)$ on the open domain $D$
([[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]],
[[def-maximal-ode-solution]]). A $D$-maximal motion is a restriction of a
supplier motion of the full force model, but its maximal interval need not be
maximal for the full domain $D_0$. The model is **autonomous** when
$I_0=\mathbb R$, $D=\mathbb R\times S_0$ for an open **state domain**
$S_0\subseteq Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, and $F$ is independent of $t$. It is
**$P$-periodic**, for $P>0$, when $I_0=\mathbb R$, $D$ is invariant under
$(t,x,v)\mapsto(t+P,x,v)$ in both directions, and
$F(t+P,x,v)=F(t,x,v)$ on $D$. Thus every integer shift by $P$ preserves the
time and state domain used by the model. All time intervals use the frame-time
parameter fixed by [[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]] with $[t]=\tau$
([[def-cm01-units]]).

**(ii) Associated field and flow.** Write $n:=3N$; the state curve
$z:=(x,x')$ of a motion is a solution of $z'=Z(t,z)$ and
conversely ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] clause (c)). For an autonomous model
write $G:S_0\to\mathbb R^{6N}$, $G(x,v):=(v,\mathsf M^{-1}F(x,v))$; by the
standing regularity of $F$, the field $G$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz
in the state, so it has a **local flow**
$$\Phi:\Omega\longrightarrow S_0,\qquad \Phi(t,z_0):=z(t;z_0),$$
with maximal solutions $z(\,\cdot\,;z_0):I_{z_0}\to S_0$ and flow domain
$\Omega=\{(t,z_0):t\in I_{z_0}\}$, in the sense of
[[def-cm-local-flow-of-an-autonomous-system]]. The model's motions with state
curve through $z_0$ at time $0$ are exactly the curves $t\mapsto\Phi(t,z_0)$
restricted to their maximal intervals, and
$\Phi(s+t,z_0)=\Phi(t,\Phi(s,z_0))$ wherever both sides are defined
([[lem-cm-local-flow-composition-law]]). If in addition $F$ is of class $C^1$
in the state, then $\Omega$ is open and $\Phi$ is $C^1$ on it
([[cor-cm-flow-domain-open-and-flow-is-c1]]). No completeness of $\Phi$ is
asserted: the maximal interval $I_{z_0}$ may be bounded
([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]).

Declare the one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and potential
$U(t,x):=\tfrac12k\bigl(x_{1}-v_{0}t-c\bigr)^{2}$ with constants $k>0$,
$v_{0}\in\mathbb R$ and $c\in\mathbb R$, and no residual forces: the label is
attached by a spring of stiffness $k$ to a support whose position is the
prescribed function $v_{0}t+c$, so the force map is
$F=\bigl(-k(x_{1}-v_{0}t-c),0,0\bigr)$ and the mechanical Lagrangian is
$L=K-U$ with $K(v)=\tfrac12m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}$
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). Introduce the **co-moving
coordinates**
$X(t,y):=\bigl(y_{1}+v_{0}t+c,\ y_{2},\ y_{3}\bigr)$, a time-dependent
coordinate map with $X_{q}=I_{3}$, and the substituted Lagrangian
$L'(t,y,w):=L\bigl(t,X(t,y),\,X_{t}(t,y)+X_{q}(t,y)w\bigr)$. This $L'$ is a generic fibre-full time-dependent Lagrangian chart of [[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]]; it need not be a $K-U$ presentation in a static coordinate map. The model units are $[k]=\mu\tau^{-2}$ (newtons per metre), $[v_0]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (metres per second), $[c]=[y_0]=\ell$ (metres), $[q]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$ (momentum, kilograms metres per second), and $[\omega]=\tau^{-1}$ (radians per second with dimensionless radians). Here $y_0$ and $q$ are initial co-moving position and first momentum, respectively. Then:
 
1. $L'(t,y,w)=\tfrac12m\bigl(w_{1}+v_{0}\bigr)^{2}+\tfrac12m\bigl(w_{2}^{2}+w_{3}^{2}\bigr)-\tfrac12ky_{1}^{2}$,
   its fibre derivative is
   $$p'=L'_{w}(t,y,w)=\bigl(m(w_{1}+v_{0}),\ mw_{2},\ mw_{3}\bigr),$$
   and the coordinate change reproduces the model's equation: a $C^{2}$ curve
   $y$ satisfies the Euler-Lagrange equation of $L'$ exactly when
   $x(t)=X(t,y(t))$ satisfies $m\ddot x_{1}=-k(x_{1}-v_{0}t-c)$, $m\ddot x_{2}=m\ddot x_{3}=0$
   ([[pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-equations]]).
2. $L'$ is hyperregular on its chart with inverse branch
   $w=\bigl(p'_{1}/m-v_{0},\ p'_{2}/m,\ p'_{3}/m\bigr)$ and Hamiltonian
   $$H'(t,y,p')=\frac{p'_{1}{}^{2}}{2m}-v_{0}p'_{1}+\frac{p'_{2}{}^{2}}{2m}+\frac{p'_{3}{}^{2}}{2m}+\frac{k}{2}y_{1}^{2} =\frac{\bigl(p'_{1}-mv_{0}\bigr)^{2}}{2m}+\frac{k}{2}y_{1}^{2}+\frac{p'_{2}{}^{2}+p'_{3}{}^{2}}{2m}-\frac{mv_{0}^{2}}{2},$$
   so that on the first coordinate the momentum $p'_{1}$ equals the inertial
   momentum $p_{1}=m\dot x_{1}$ of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]] while the
   branch velocity is shifted,
   $\dot y_{1}=p'_{1}/m-v_{0}$.
3. Hamilton's equations of $H'$ are
   $\dot y_{1}=p'_{1}/m-v_{0}$, $\dot p'_{1}=-ky_{1}$, $\dot y_{i}=p'_{i}/m$,
   $\dot p'_{i}=0$ for $i=2,3$; they imply $m\ddot y_{1}=-ky_{1}$, equivalently
   $m\ddot x_{1}=-k(x_{1}-v_{0}t-c)$, so the co-moving description is
   equivalent to the model's motion and the induced curve $x$ is a motion
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]).
4. along the solutions the Hamiltonian $H'$ is conserved — it has no explicit
   time dependence in the co-moving chart — while the model's mechanical
   energy $E=K+U$ obeys, on the first axis,
   $$H'=E-v_{0}p'_{1},\qquad E'(t)=-kv_{0}y_{1}(t).$$
   At any time when $v_{0}y_{1}(t)\neq0$, the energy derivative is nonzero;
   in particular, the displayed solution has nonconstant $E$ when
   $v_{0}y_{0}\neq0$. With data $y_{1}(0)=y_{0}$, $p'_{1}(0)=q$ and
   $\omega:=\sqrt{k/m}$ the explicit solution is
   $$y_{1}(t)=y_{0}\cos\omega t+\frac{q-mv_{0}}{m\omega}\sin\omega t,\qquad p'_{1}(t)=-m\omega y_{0}\sin\omega t+\bigl(q-mv_{0}\bigr)\cos\omega t+mv_{0}.$$
 
All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; the moving
support is a prescribed external mechanism, and no measurement is reported.

**Given:** The one-label model with the moving-support spring potential, the co-moving coordinate map $X$, the substituted Lagrangian $L'$ with its momentum $p'$ and Hamiltonian $H'$, and the initial data $y_{0},q$ of clause 4.
 
[F1] Model and Lagrangian data ([[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], [[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]], [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]): the model has $L=K-U$ with $K(v)=\tfrac12m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}$, $U$ of class $C^{2}$, no residual forces, and motions solving $m\ddot x_{i}=F_{i}(t,x,\dot x)$; dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]].
 
[F2] Rheonomic coordinate covariance ([[pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-equations]], [[pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations]]): for a $C^{3}$ coordinate map $X(t,q)$ with invertible $X_{q}$ and substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L(t,q,v)=L(t,X,X_{t}+X_{q}v)$, one has $E_{\widetilde L}(q)=X_{q}^{\mathsf T}E_{L}(x)$ along induced curves, so the substituted Euler-Lagrange equation is equivalent to the model's potential-part equation.
 
[F3] Hyperregularity and branch Hamiltonian ([[prop-cm-mechanical-chart-lagrangian-is-hyperregular]], [[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]], [[def-invertible-euclidean-linear-map]], [[def-linear-map]], [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]): a fibre-full $C^{2}$ chart of the form $\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}Gv+A\cdot v-V$ with $G$ symmetric positive definite has fibre derivative $Gv+A$, is hyperregular with inverse $v=G^{-1}(p-A)$, and has branch Hamiltonian $\tfrac12(p-A)\cdot G^{-1}(p-A)+V$.
